elements.element: Customer owns all deliverables created for it.
elements.evidence: The clause does not address deliverables or vest ownership of them in Customer; it instead provides for joint ownership of jointly created intellectual property.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for it.
elements.evidence: The clause does not address work product or vest ownership of it in Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer its rights in deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment of deliverables from Vendor to Customer is included.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer its rights in work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: No assignment of work product from Vendor to Customer is included.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no ownership reservation for Vendor's pre-existing intellectual property.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor intellectual property embedded in the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in deliverables is granted to Customer. The clause only gives each party rights concerning jointly owned intellectual property within its own territory.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No embedded-IP licence or perpetual duration is stated.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No embedded-IP licence or irrevocability protection is stated.

elements.element: The licence to embedded Vendor intellectual property is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No embedded-IP licence or royalty-free term is stated.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed, and no reservation of Customer's rights in such data is included.

elements.element: There is no joint ownership of intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section (c) expressly states that jointly made know-how, inventions, and other intellectual property shall be jointly owned by the parties or their respective Affiliates.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause does not address generic tools or assign ownership of them to Vendor.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not establish Vendor ownership of its know-how generally and expressly makes jointly created know-how jointly owned.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence to the deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables is granted to Customer; only rights concerning jointly owned intellectual property are addressed.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables or perpetual duration is stated.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables or irrevocability protection is stated.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables is granted, and the exploitation rights that are granted are expressly limited to each party's own territory.

elements.element: The licence to the deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No licence to deliverables or royalty-free term is stated.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to use the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The clause does not grant Customer a right to use deliverables for its business. The right to practice jointly owned intellectual property is limited to each party's own territory.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to modify the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: No right to modify deliverables is included.

elements.element: The licence permits Customer to sublicense the deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Although each party may grant licences under jointly owned intellectual property within its own territory, no right is granted to Customer to sublicense deliverables for its business.

result.reason: The redline retains the expressly disallowed joint-ownership structure and merely expands each party's territorial exploitation and licensing rights. It does not establish Customer ownership of deliverables or work product, protect Customer Data, provide an assignment, reserve pre-existing Vendor IP, or grant the required embedded-IP or deliverables licences. It therefore reaches neither the preferred nor fallback position and adds a territorial joint-IP regime that does not implement the stated rule.
